formalization.project_name: Kuratowski–Ulam category theorem for countable pi-base spaces

mathematical_sources.note: Directly consulted author manuscript, PDF SHA256 61dd303285ff45d400e12ea083611f9ca6cc67cd49070f173fee02314f0e67fc. Introduction printed p.1 recalls the classical nowhere-dense section theorem for arbitrary first factor and second factor of countable pi-weight; pp.1–2 recall and explain the meagre-section consequence. The original Kuratowski–Ulam paper is not claimed consulted. This package proves those section properties, not the paper’s stronger I-favorable-space, hyperspace or game-theoretic results. The Baire-property converse and product-Baire theorem are explicitly proved companion results. No novelty, priority or first-formalization claim.
mathematical_sources.title: Game Approach to Universally Kuratowski-Ulam Spaces, arXiv:math/0605469v1

mathematical_sources.note: Directly consulted author manuscript, PDF SHA256 9608db539b8e5f460ea9a61e78b8ac5164f238624e40f1edd4c59ce48a60515f. Section2 printed p.3 independently recalls the countable-pi-weight nowhere-dense section theorem and explains pi-bases, establishing continuing research relevance. Its stronger game results and CCC standing scope are not imported as claims or assumptions. The papers differ in naming uK-U versus uK-U-star; this package states literal section properties rather than conflating those names.
mathematical_sources.title: Universally Kuratowski-Ulam spaces and open-open games, arXiv:1202.2056v3

related_formalizations.note: Uses canonical IsNowhereDense, IsMeagre, residual filters, countable intersections, actual product topology and open coordinate projections. Mathlib BaireMeasurableSet is the property of Baire (open modulo meagre), not the separate Baire sigma-algebra generated by continuous functions; its residualEq_isOpen bridge and Baire category lemmas are credited. No equivalent section theorem was located in bounded pinned-library audit. The substantive new bridge constructs a countable family of projected dense open sets and assembles generic-section implications.
